newsitem.title: LIECHTENSTEIN: LGT gets ratings from Moody's, S&P.
newsitem.headline: LGT gets ratings from Moody's, S&P.

text.p: LGT Bank in Liechtenstein said it has received ratings from Moody's and Standard & Poor's for its short- and long-term debt.
The bank said with the announcement that it expected a good result for 1996, and added that it expected current low level of interest rates to continue in 1997.
LGT said it received ratings of Prime-1 and A-1+, from Moody's and S&P respectively, for its short-term debt paper, and ratings of Aa3 and AA-/stable, respectively for its long-term debt paper.

"These ratings offer an independent and neutral valuation of the creditworthiness of LGT Bank in Liechtenstein. They are also a prerequisite for the bank's entry into U.S. capital markets, and offer an additional security and quality standard with respect to business ties with LGT," the bank said in a statement to announce the ratings.
At the same time, the Principality of Liechtenstein received a triple A rating from both agencies, LGT said.
The 75-year old bank is a member of Liechtenstein Global Trust, a group which includes GT Global, the U.S.-based fund manager.
The group also purchased U.S. fund manager Chancellor Capital Managment this autumn.
For the LGT bank alone, customer assets under management and advisement totaled roughly 26 billion Swiss francs at the end of September, the bank said.
